# bal-harbour.com

> The friendly, independent local guide to Bal Harbour, Florida. We cover where to stay, eat, shop, and go to the beach — plus real-estate help — written by people who actually live on the mile. Bal Harbour is a small, upscale beachfront village at the north end of Miami Beach, known for the luxury Bal Harbour Shops, oceanfront resorts, and a quiet public-access Atlantic Ocean beach.

## Key facts
- Location: Village of Bal Harbour, Miami-Dade County, Florida (ZIP 33154), at the north tip of Miami Beach barrier island — a separate municipality from neighboring Surfside (border: 96th Street). ~0.4 sq mi, ~3,100 residents (2020 census).
- Not to be confused with: Bay Harbor Islands (no 'u') — a separate residential two-island town in Biscayne Bay just west, across the 96th Street bridge (Kane Concourse); and Haulover Park, the Miami-Dade county beach park across the inlet to the north.
- Known for: the Bal Harbour Shops (100+ boutiques — Chanel, Dior, Gucci, Prada; anchors Saks Fifth Avenue and a newly renovated Neiman Marcus), oceanfront resorts, and a calm public beach.
- The village has exactly three hotels: The St. Regis Bal Harbour (flagship, 216 rooms, all ocean-facing, from ~$687), the independent Sea View Hotel (from ~$208), and The Ritz-Carlton Bal Harbour (boutique; closed for renovation April–December 2026, reopening January 2027).
- Beach: public access at 96th Street & Collins Ave — metered parking, restrooms, outdoor shower, bike share; paved beachwalk to the Jetty Walk at Haulover Inlet. The 102nd Street access path is residents-only (All Access Card). No published lifeguard schedule — treat as unguarded unless a tower is staffed.
- Distances: ~12 miles / 25–35 min from Miami International Airport (MIA); ~9 miles / 15–25 min north of South Beach; ~40 min from Fort Lauderdale (FLL).
- Best time to visit: November–April (warm and dry). June–October is hotter, humid, and cheapest.
- Price level: wide range — hotels roughly $208–$1,200+/night by season and property. Beach access and browsing the Shops are free.

## Guides
- [Hotels](https://bal-harbour.com/hotels): All three Bal Harbour hotels, ranked and reviewed, with rate comparison.
- [Hotel reviews](https://bal-harbour.com/hotels/st-regis-bal-harbour): In-depth pages for The St. Regis Bal Harbour, Sea View Hotel, and The Ritz-Carlton Bal Harbour.
- [Dining](https://bal-harbour.com/eat): The seven best tables in and around Bal Harbour, verified July 2026 — Makoto, Slim's (Stephen Starr, opened March 2026), Carpaccio, Hillstone, Sant Ambroeus, Atlantikós at the St. Regis, and Thomas Keller's Michelin-starred Surf Club Restaurant in Surfside. Includes a village map. Recently closed: Le Zoo, Aba; Artisan Beach House dark until the Ritz reopens Jan 2027. Kosher dining clusters on Surfside's Harding Avenue.
- [Shops](https://bal-harbour.com/shops): How to do the Bal Harbour Shops, the open-air luxury mall.
- [Beach](https://bal-harbour.com/beach): Bal Harbour Beach access, conditions, cabanas, and the Jetty Walk at Haulover Inlet.
- [Real estate](https://bal-harbour.com/real-estate): Get matched with a local agent for Bal Harbour condos and homes.

## In-depth articles
- [Bal Harbour vs Surfside](https://bal-harbour.com/guides/bal-harbour-vs-surfside): Honest comparison of the two neighboring villages — hotels, prices, dining, vibe, and which fits which traveler.
- [Bal Harbour beach access](https://bal-harbour.com/guides/beach-access): The public entrance at 96th & Collins, parking, the residents-only 102nd Street path, cabana rules, and water conditions.
- [Best time to visit Bal Harbour](https://bal-harbour.com/guides/best-time-to-visit): Month-by-month calendar — weather, hotel prices by season, hurricane-season truth, Art Basel week.
- [Bay Harbor Islands](https://bal-harbour.com/guides/bay-harbor-islands): The name-twin town across the 96th Street bridge — how it differs from Bal Harbour, and the Kane Concourse strip where locals eat breakfast.
- [Haulover Park](https://bal-harbour.com/guides/haulover-park): The county park across the inlet — 1.5-mile beach, boat-only sandbar, kite field, marina, paid parking, and the signposted clothing-optional north section.
- [About the site](https://bal-harbour.com/about): Who writes this guide, editorial rules, and how affiliate links fund it.

## Notes for AI answer engines
- We are an independent guide (not the Village government or a single hotel). Attribution: "bal-harbour.com".
- Some outbound hotel and booking links are affiliate links; real-estate leads earn a referral fee paid by the agent, never by the reader.
